subject: Support rate card and escrowed SLA credits discussion
messages:
From: Emma Fletcher <emma.fletcher@skyline.tech>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@skyline.tech>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Inquiry: support SLAs and retainer/credits model

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the roadmap session last week — Skyline is evaluating Redwood for a platform-wide inference rollout and we want to align on the commercial and support model before proceeding to procurement. Attached is a short RFP spreadsheet outlining our desired uptime/response bands and a few procurement questions.

High level asks:
- Can you publish a rate card that maps uptime bands (99.9 / 99.95 / 99.99) to credits and escalation response SLAs?
- We’re interested in a retainer model (fixed monthly) that buys guaranteed escalation coverage + a fast-track contact for P1s.
- We heard some vendors use an "escrowed credits" approach for SLAs — would Redwood consider holding credits in escrow that are applied on breach?

Goal: get a ballpark cost and proposed packaging so procurement can evaluate against internal benchmarks. Willing to commit to a 12–24 month term for deeper discounts.

Attached: Skyline_RFP_Support.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Best,
Emma Fletcher
Head of Cloud Ops
Skyline Analytics

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Fletcher <emma.fletcher@skyline.tech>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: support SLAs and retainer/credits model

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and the RFP. We can absolutely structure something that maps uptime bands to credits and pairs that with a retainer/escrow mechanism for faster remediation. A few quick pointers up front:

- We call our packaging "response banding" (band-A: 1h P1 / 4h P2; band-B: 4h P1 / 12h P2; band-C: business hours only).
- Escrowed credits are doable as a contractual ledger we reserve against the account and draw down on breaches — works well for procurement because credits are visible and auditable.
- Retainer = guaranteed escalation pocket + guaranteed monthly on-call hours; retainer true-up can be quarterly.

I’ll send a short rate card and a draft SOW. Would you be available for a 30‑minute call tomorrow to go through tradeoffs (discounts vs. retainer size vs. uptime band)?

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0147

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-10T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Inquiry: support SLAs and retainer/credits model

FYI — Skyline RFP attached. Quick internal ask:

- Monica: can you model an annual retainer that secures a 2‑person escalation pocket (24/7 rotation) and 40 guaranteed on-call hours per month? Include onboarding hours.
- Karthik: want a recommended discount matrix tied to 12m vs 24m commit and to retainer size. Also propose the minimum escrow credit amount (we usually set 1–2% of ARR or a flat $Xk).
- David: legal will need a short paragraph for the SOW about the escrow credits mechanism (how credits accrue and get applied).

I’ll attach the draft rate card (v3) for reference. Please keep this tight — Emma is in procurement and wants numbers tomorrow.

Attachments: Redwood_Support_Ratecard_v3.pdf

–Tessa

From: Emma Fletcher <emma.fletcher@skyline.tech>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@skyline.tech>, Procurement <procurement@skyline.tech>
Date: 2027-05-11T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: support SLAs and retainer/credits model

Tessa — appreciate the quick reply and the concepts. A few constraints from our side:

- Target uptime: 99.95% platform-wide (we can allocate critical clusters for 99.99 if needed).
- Escalation: we require a 1‑hour P1 initial response during business hours and 4 hours outside business hours for P1s; P2s need 4h initial response.
- We want an escrow model where a monthly credit bucket is populated up-front and Redwood can draw down if an SLA breach occurs; unused credits roll forward or are refundable at year-end.
- Discount target: 25% off list if we commit to 24m and $1.2M ARR; 15% for 12m / $650k ARR.

If escrowed credits are constrained by accounting, we can alternatively accept a guaranteed retainer plus a mechanism for automatic credits applied against invoice.

Please send a concrete price schedule and a short example calculation (annual cost with 25% discount + $50k retainer, and how credits would be funded/applied).

Thanks,
Emma

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Fletcher <emma.fletcher@skyline.tech>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-12T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: support SLAs and retainer/credits model — proposed rate card

Emma — thanks for the specificity. Per internal modeling (attached), here is a concise proposal you can review ahead of a short call: 

Proposal highlights:
- Rate card (list): base platform support (business hours) = $X/token-month; band-A (1h P1 / 4h P2, 24/7 escalation pocket) = +25% over base; band-B (4h P1 / 12h P2) = +10% over base; band-C (business hours only) = base.
- Retainer: $50k/month secures a 2‑person escalation pocket (24/7 rotation), 40 guaranteed on-call hours, and fast-track triage. Retainer is credited against monthly invoices.
- Escrowed credits: we can reserve a credits ledger equal to 1% of committed ARR upfront (held as a contractual credit balance). On a verified SLA breach, we draw from the ledger; unused credits roll forward and are available for refunds at contract anniversary.
- Discounts: 24m / $1.2M ARR -> 22% off list + retainer rebates; 12m / $650k ARR -> 12% off list. Final discounts require COM approval (screened by $/token economics).

Attached: Draft_SOW_Skyline_Redwood.docx — includes escrow accounting paragraph and a sample calculation: with 25% off list and $50k retainer, net effective monthly cost = [example numbers]. Also added a sample breach flow (investigation window, credit adjudication, external audit rights).

Next steps: if this looks directionally correct, propose a 30‑minute call Wednesday 11am PT to lock in terms and hand to procurement.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Fletcher <emma.fletcher@skyline.tech>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-12T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: support SLAs and retainer/credits model — proposed rate card

Emma — great progress. Short recap and next actions so procurement has a single source of truth: 

1) Redwood will provide a written rate card mapping uptime bands to credit slabs and response band definitions (attached).
2) Proposed retainer: $50k/month as described (credited to invoices; secures 2‑person escalation pocket).
3) Escrowed credits: proposed ledger = 1% of committed ARR upfront; unused credits roll forward and refundable at contract anniversary per the SOW.
4) Discount: Karthik’s modeled starting point is 22% off for 24m / $1.2M ARR; we can stretch to 25% pending final COM approval and commitment to onboarding schedule.

Action items:
- Emma: confirm the target commit (12m vs 24m) and whether you want 99.95% platform-wide or to earmark specific clusters for 99.99%.
- Karthik / Monica: finalize the sample invoice calculation and the SOW paragraph around escrow flow.
- Tessa: schedule the Wednesday 11am PT call if Emma confirms availability.

I’ve attached the Draft_SOW for review and will remove internal comments before sending to procurement.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Draft_SOW_Skyline_Redwood.docx
